Document: Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents
Section: Settlement
Part 4 of 4
==================================================
## Settlement

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] 7.47 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraphs 7.49 and 7.50 apply, the defendant must pay—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (1) the agreed damages less any—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (a) deductible amount which is payable to the CRU; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (b) previous interim payment;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (2) any unpaid Stage 1 fixed costs in Table 10 in Practice Direction 45;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (3) the Stage 2 fixed costs in Table 10 in Practice Direction 45;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (4) where an additional advice on quantum of damages is justified under paragraph 7.10, a sum equal to the Type C fixed costs to cover the cost of that advice;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (5) the relevant disbursements allowed in accordance with rule 45.58 including any disbursements fixed under rule 45.62(2); and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (6) where applicable, any success fee in accordance with rule 45.31(1) (as it was in force immediately before 1 April 2013),

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] within 10 days of the parties agreeing a settlement.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (Rule 21.10 provides that the approval of the court is required where, before proceedings are started, a claim is made by a child and a settlement is reached.  The provisions in paragraph 6.1 of Practice Direction 49F set out what must be filed with the court when an application is made to approve a settlement.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] 7.48 Except where paragraph 7.51 applies, where the parties agree a settlement for a greater sum than the defendant had offered during the total consideration period or further consideration period and after the Court Proceedings Pack has been sent to the defendant but before proceedings are issued under Stage 3—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (1) paragraph 7.47 applies; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (2) the defendant must also pay the fixed late settlement costs in rule 45.33.

## Application for certificate of recoverable benefits

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Application for certificate of recoverable benefits] 7.49 Paragraph 7.50 applies where, at the date of the acceptance of an offer in the Stage 2 Settlement Pack, the defendant does not have a certificate of recoverable benefits that will remain in force for at least 10 days.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Application for certificate of recoverable benefits] 7.50 The defendant should apply for a fresh certificate of recoverable benefits as soon as possible, notify the claimant that it has done so and must pay the amounts set out in paragraph 7.47 within 30 days of the end of the relevant period in paragraphs 7.35 to 7.37.

## Vehicle related damages – additional damages

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Vehicle related damages – additional damages] 7.51 Paragraph 7.52 applies where at the end of the relevant period in paragraphs 7.35 to 7.37 the claim (“the original damages”) has not settled and there remain vehicle related damages (“the additional damages”) being dealt with by a third party separate from the claim.  The original damages include all elements of the claim in the existing Stage 2 Settlement Pack.

## 7.52 Where paragraph 7.51 applies the claimant must, in relation to the additional damages—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.52 Where paragraph 7.51 applies the claimant must, in relation to the additional damages—] (1) notify the defendant that this separate claim is being considered;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.52 Where paragraph 7.51 applies the claimant must, in relation to the additional damages—] (2) obtain all relevant information from the third party; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.52 Where paragraph 7.51 applies the claimant must, in relation to the additional damages—] (3) make a separate offer by amending the Stage 2 Settlement Pack Form.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.52 Where paragraph 7.51 applies the claimant must, in relation to the additional damages—] 7.53 Within 15 days of the claimant sending the offer under paragraph 7.52(3), the defendant must either agree the offer made by the claimant or make a counter-offer.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.52 Where paragraph 7.51 applies the claimant must, in relation to the additional damages—] 7.54 The counter offer must explain why a particular head of damage has been reduced to assist the claimant when negotiating a settlement and to allow both parties to focus on those areas of the claim that remain in dispute.

## Original damages and additional damages are agreed

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Original damages and additional damages are agreed] 7.55 Where the original damages and additional damages are agreed within the period in paragraph 7.53 the defendant must pay the claimant in accordance with paragraph 7.62.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Original damages and additional damages are agreed] 7.56 Where the parties agree a settlement for a greater sum than the Defendant had offered during the period in paragraph 7.53 but after the Court Proceedings  Pack has been sent to the Defendant and before proceedings are issued under Stage 3,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Original damages and additional damages are agreed] (1)  paragraph 7.55 applies; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Original damages and additional damages are agreed] (2)  the defendant must also pay the fixed late settlement costs in rule 45.33.

## Original damages are not agreed, additional damages are agreed

## 7.57 Paragraph 7.58 applies where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.57 Paragraph 7.58 applies where—] (1) the original damages are not agreed; but

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.57 Paragraph 7.58 applies where—] (2) the additional damages are agreed.

## 7.58 Where paragraph 7.57 applies—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.58 Where paragraph 7.57 applies—] (1) the defendant must pay the agreed amount of the additional damages within 10 days of agreeing those damages, and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.58 Where paragraph 7.57 applies—] (2) the claimant must continue with the provisions in paragraphs 7.64 to 7.75 of this Protocol.

## Original damages are agreed, additional damages are not agreed

## 7.59 Paragraph 7.60 applies where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.59 Paragraph 7.60 applies where—] (1) the original damages are agreed; but

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.59 Paragraph 7.60 applies where—] (2) the additional damages are not agreed.

## 7.60 Where paragraph 7.59 applies—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.60 Where paragraph 7.59 applies—] (1) the defendant must, in relation to the original damages, pay the claimant in accordance with paragraph 7.62; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.60 Where paragraph 7.59 applies—] (2) the claimant may start proceedings under Part 7 of the CPR in relation to the additional damages.

## Original damages and additional damages are not agreed

## 7.61 Paragraphs 7.70 to 7.75 apply where the original and additional damages are not agreed.

## Settlement after claim for additional damages

## 7.62 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraph 7.64 applies, the defendant must pay—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.62 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraph 7.64 applies, the defendant must pay—] (1) the agreed damages less any—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.62 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraph 7.64 applies, the defendant must pay—] (a) deductible amount which is payable to the CRU; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.62 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraph 7.64 applies, the defendant must pay—] (b) previous interim payment;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.62 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraph 7.64 applies, the defendant must pay—] (2) any unpaid Stage 1 fixed costs in Table 10 in Practice Direction 45;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.62 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraph 7.64 applies, the defendant must pay—] (3) the Stage 2 fixed costs in Table 10 in Practice Direction 45;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.62 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraph 7.64 applies, the defendant must pay—] (4) where an additional advice on quantum of damages is justified under paragraph 7.10, a sum equal to the Type C fixed costs to cover the costs of that advice;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.62 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraph 7.64 applies, the defendant must pay—] (5) the relevant disbursements allowed in accordance with rule 45.58 including any disbursements fixed under rule 45.62(2); and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.62 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraph 7.64 applies, the defendant must pay—] (6)    where applicable, any success fee in accordance with rule 45.31 (as it was in force immediately before 1 April 2013)  for Stage 1 and Stage 2 fixed costs, within 10 days of agreeing to pay the damages.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.62 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraph 7.64 applies, the defendant must pay—] (Rule 21.10 provides that the approval of the court is required where, before proceedings are started, a claim is made by a child and a settlement is reached. The provisions in paragraph 6.1 of Practice Direction 49F set out what must be filed with the court when an application is made to approve a settlement.)

## Application for certificate of recoverable benefits

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Application for certificate of recoverable benefits] 7.63 Where at the date on which damages are agreed the defendant does not have a certificate of recoverable benefits that remains in force for at least 10 days the defendant should apply for a fresh certificate as soon as possible, notify the claimant that it has done so and must pay the amounts set out in paragraph 7.62 within 30 days of the date on which damages are agreed.

## Failure to reach agreement – general

## 7.64 Where the parties do not reach an agreement on

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.64 Where the parties do not reach an agreement on] (1) the original damages within the periods specified in paragraphs 7.35 to 7.37; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.64 Where the parties do not reach an agreement on] (2) the original damages and, where relevant, the additional damages under paragraph 7.51,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.64 Where the parties do not reach an agreement on] the claimant must send to the defendant the Court Proceedings Pack (Part A and Part B) Form which must contain—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.64 Where the parties do not reach an agreement on] (a) in Part A, the final schedule of the claimant’s losses and the defendant’s responses comprising only the figures specified in subparagraphs (1) and (2) above, together with supporting comments and evidence from both parties on any disputed heads of damage; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.64 Where the parties do not reach an agreement on] (b) in Part B, the final offer and counter offer from the Stage 2 Settlement Pack Form and, where relevant, the offer and any final counter offer made under paragraph 7.53.

## 7.65 The deductible amount should only be deducted from the personal injury damages.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.65 The deductible amount should only be deducted from the personal injury damages.] 7.66 Comments in the Court Proceedings Pack (Part A) Form must not raise anything that has not been raised in the Stage 2 Settlement Pack Form.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.65 The deductible amount should only be deducted from the personal injury damages.] 7.67 The defendant should then check that the Court Proceedings Pack (Part A and Part B) Form complies with paragraphs 7.64 to 7.66. If the defendant considers that the Court Proceedings Pack (Part A and Part B) Form does not comply it must be returned to the claimant within 5 days with an explanation as to why it does not comply.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.65 The deductible amount should only be deducted from the personal injury damages.] 7.68 Where the defendant intends to nominate a legal representative to accept service the name and address of the legal representative should be provided in the Court Proceedings Pack (Part A) Form.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.65 The deductible amount should only be deducted from the personal injury damages.] 7.69 Where the defendant fails to return the Court Proceedings Pack (Part A and Part B) Form within the period in paragraph 7.67, the claimant should assume that the defendant has no further comment to make.

## Non-settlement payment by the defendant at the end of Stage 2

## 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—] (1) the final offer of damages made by the defendant in the Court Proceedings Pack (Part A and Part B) Form less any—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—] (a) deductible amount which is payable to the CRU; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—] (b) previous interim payment;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—] (2) any unpaid Stage 1 fixed costs in Table 10 in Practice Direction 45;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—] (3) the Stage 2 fixed costs in Table 10 in Practice Direction 45; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—] (4) the disbursements in rule 45.58 that have been agreed including any disbursements fixed under rule 45.62(2).

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—] 7.71 Where the amount of a disbursement is not agreed the defendant must pay such amount for the disbursement as the defendant considers reasonable.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—] 7.72 Subject to paragraphs 7.73 and 7.74 the defendant must pay the amounts in paragraph 7.70 and 7.71 within 15 days of receiving the Court Proceedings Pack (Part A and Part B) Form from the claimant.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—] 7.73 Paragraph 7.74 applies where the defendant is required to make the payments in paragraph 7.70 but does not have a certificate of recoverable benefits that remains in force for at least 10 days.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—] 7.74 The defendant should apply for a fresh certificate of recoverable benefits as soon as possible, notify the claimant that it has done so and must pay the amounts set out in paragraph 7.70 within 30 days of receiving the Court Proceedings Pack (Part A and Part B) Form from the claimant.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.70 Except where the claimant is a child the defendant must pay to the claimant—] 7.75 Where the defendant does not comply with paragraphs 7.72 or 7.74 the claimant may give written notice that the claim will no longer continue under this Protocol and start proceedings under Part 7 of the CPR.

## General provisions

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > General provisions] 7.76 Where the claimant gives notice to the defendant that the claim is unsuitable for this Protocol (for example, because there are complex issues of fact or law) then the claim will no longer continue under this Protocol.  However, where the court considers that the claimant acted unreasonably in giving such notice it will award no more than the applicable fixed costs in rule 45.28(a)

## Stage 3

## Stage 3 Procedure

## 8.1 The Stage 3 Procedure is set out in Practice Direction 49F.
